const r=await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /private/tmp/append_week3_experiments.py <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import nbformat as nbf

path = Path('/Users/raimova-al/Documents/study/master/res_sys/llm-4-res-sys/week3/movie_lens_eda.ipynb')
nb = nbf.read(str(path), as_version=4)
if any('## Reproducible collaborative-filtering experiment' in cell.source for cell in nb.cells):
    raise SystemExit('Experiment section already exists')

nb.cells += [
    nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell('''## Reproducible collaborative-filtering experiment

This section evaluates **three user-based CF similarity methods** and a separate **matrix-factorization benchmark** on the same MovieLens ratings. All methods use the same catalog, users, and held-out pairs. For each user, ratings are ordered by `(timestamp, item_id)`; the earliest 70% train the models, the next 15% form validation, and the rest form the untouched test set. Item ID breaks equal-timestamp ties deterministically. We do **not** refit on validation after tuning, so every final model uses only the original train partition.

The implementation is in `evaluation.py`; focused checks are in `test_evaluation.py`. Numeric outputs below are produced by running the code, not entered by hand.'''),
    nbf.v4.new_code_cell('''import platform
import subprocess
import sys

experiment_dir = next((folder for folder in [Path.cwd(), Path("llm-4-res-sys/week3")]
                       if (folder / "evaluation.py").is_file()), None)
if experiment_dir is None:
    raise FileNotFoundError("Run from the repository root or llm-4-res-sys/week3")
if str(experiment_dir.resolve()) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(experiment_dir.resolve()))
import evaluation as ev

train_ratings, validation_ratings, test_ratings = ev.chronological_split(ratings)
train_data = ev.build_training_data(train_ratings, ratings.user_id.unique(), items.item_id)
train_pairs = set(zip(train_ratings.user_id, train_ratings.item_id))
validation_pairs = set(zip(validation_ratings.user_id, validation_ratings.item_id))
test_pairs = set(zip(test_ratings.user_id, test_ratings.item_id))
assert train_pairs.isdisjoint(validation_pairs)
assert train_pairs.isdisjoint(test_pairs)
assert validation_pairs.isdisjoint(test_pairs)
assert len(train_ratings) + len(validation_ratings) + len(test_ratings) == len(ratings)

print(f"Python {platform.python_version()}, NumPy {np.__version__}, pandas {pd.__version__}")
print(f"Train: {len(train_ratings):,}; validation: {len(validation_ratings):,}; test: {len(test_ratings):,}")
print(f"Users: {len(train_data.user_ids):,}; catalog movies: {len(train_data.item_ids):,}")
print(f"Relevant validation ratings (>=4): {(validation_ratings.rating >= 4).sum():,}")
print(f"Relevant test ratings (>=4): {(test_ratings.rating >= 4).sum():,}")
print("Split overlap checks passed; every method will use these same partitions.")'''),
    nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell('''### Prediction and ranking protocol

All three neighborhood methods use **cosine similarity**, select the same number *K* of positive-similarity neighbors, and predict an unseen rating as

`sum(similarity(user, neighbor) × neighbor's observed rating) / sum(similarity(user, neighbor))`,

where the sums include only selected neighbors who actually rated that candidate. Mean-imputed and factorized values affect similarity only: they are never treated as observed neighbor ratings or as items the target user consumed. If no selected neighbor rated the candidate, the fallback is its **train item mean**; if that item has no train ratings, it is the **train user mean** (or train global mean for a new user). A pair with no common ratings has similarity zero. The default accepts even one common rating; common-rating weighting shrinks cosine by `min(n_common / 50, 1)`.

The factorization benchmark predicts `global mean + user bias + item bias + user factors · item factors`, trained with regularization on **observed train ratings only**. It uses the same train-derived fallback for users or items with no train history.

MAE and RMSE use identical held-out rating pairs. For ranking, every method scores the **same full catalog minus each user's train-rated items** and returns Top 10. A test rating of at least 4 is relevant. Recall@10 and binary NDCG@10 average over test users with at least one relevant test item. Missing test labels are *unknown*, not dislikes; a good unlabelled recommendation receives no credit, so these sparse-label ranking metrics are limited.

**Prediction coverage** is the fraction of test ratings scored with neighbor evidence (or trained factors), before fallback. **Recommendation coverage** is the fraction of catalog movies appearing in at least one user's Top 10. Runtime includes fitting, full-catalog scoring, and metrics; it excludes loading data and hyperparameter search.'''),
    nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell('''### Validation-only tuning

Choose one shared neighbor count for the three CF methods by the **mean validation RMSE** across them. This keeps their neighbor count identical in the final comparison. The common-rating threshold is fixed at the requested value 50 but is a configurable function argument. Factor rank and regularization are selected separately by validation RMSE. Ranking metrics are reported on test rather than used to tune these settings.'''),
    nbf.v4.new_code_cell('''common_threshold = 50
neighbor_grid = [10, 20, 40]
validation_rows = []
validation_similarity = {method: ev.user_similarity(train_data, method, common_threshold)
                         for method in ev.NEIGHBOR_METHODS}
for neighbor_count in neighbor_grid:
    for method in ev.NEIGHBOR_METHODS:
        candidate_scores, native = ev.score_neighborhood(
            train_data, validation_similarity[method], neighbor_count
        )
        measures = ev.rating_metrics(train_data, candidate_scores, native, validation_ratings)
        validation_rows.append({"neighbors": neighbor_count, "method": method,
                                "validation_MAE": measures["MAE"],
                                "validation_RMSE": measures["RMSE"]})
validation_cf = pd.DataFrame(validation_rows)
shared_neighbor_count = int(validation_cf.groupby("neighbors").validation_RMSE.mean().idxmin())
print("Shared neighbors chosen on validation:", shared_neighbor_count)
display(validation_cf.round(4))
display(validation_cf.groupby("neighbors").validation_RMSE.mean()
        .rename("mean_validation_RMSE").round(4).to_frame())'''),
    nbf.v4.new_code_cell('''factor_rows = []
factor_grid = [(rank, regularization) for rank in [8, 16]
               for regularization in [0.02, 0.10]]
for rank, regularization in factor_grid:
    config = {"rank": rank, "regularization": regularization,
              "epochs": 40, "learning_rate": 0.15, "seed": 42}
    model = ev.fit_factor_model(train_data, **config)
    candidate_scores, native = ev.score_factor_model(train_data, model)
    measures = ev.rating_metrics(train_data, candidate_scores, native, validation_ratings)
    factor_rows.append({"rank": rank, "regularization": regularization,
                        "validation_MAE": measures["MAE"],
                        "validation_RMSE": measures["RMSE"]})
validation_factor = pd.DataFrame(factor_rows).sort_values(
    ["validation_RMSE", "rank", "regularization"]
).reset_index(drop=True)
selected_factor_config = {"rank": int(validation_factor.iloc[0]["rank"]),
                          "regularization": float(validation_factor.iloc[0]["regularization"]),
                          "epochs": 40, "learning_rate": 0.15, "seed": 42}
print("Selected matrix-factorization settings:", selected_factor_config)
display(validation_factor.round(4))'''),
    nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell('''### Untouched test results

All four methods below use the same test ratings and the same eligible catalog items for each user. We fit again from the unchanged train partition using the validation-selected settings.'''),
    nbf.v4.new_code_cell('''method_names = {"co_rated": "Default: co-rated",
                "user_mean": "User mean imputation",
                "common_weight": "Common-rating weighting",
                "matrix_factorization": "Matrix factorization"}
test_rows = []
history_tables = []
for method in [*ev.NEIGHBOR_METHODS, "matrix_factorization"]:
    measures, by_history = ev.evaluate_method(
        train_data, test_ratings, method,
        neighbor_count=shared_neighbor_count,
        common_threshold=common_threshold,
        factor_config=selected_factor_config,
    )
    test_rows.append({"method": method_names[method], **measures})
    history_tables.append(by_history.assign(method=method_names[method]))
test_results = pd.DataFrame(test_rows)[
    ["method", "MAE", "RMSE", "Recall@10", "NDCG@10",
     "prediction_coverage", "recommendation_coverage", "runtime_seconds", "ranking_users"]
]
print(f"Test rating pairs: {len(test_ratings):,}; Top-10 evaluated users: {int(test_results.ranking_users.iloc[0]):,}")
display(test_results.round(4))'''),
    nbf.v4.new_code_cell('''history_results = pd.concat(history_tables, ignore_index=True)[
    ["method", "train_history", "users", "test_ratings", "RMSE", "Recall@10", "NDCG@10"]
]
print("Groups use only each user's number of TRAIN ratings; all methods share the same groups.")
display(history_results.round(4))'''),
    nbf.v4.new_code_cell('''best_rating = test_results.loc[test_results.RMSE.idxmin()]
best_ranking = test_results.loc[test_results["NDCG@10"].idxmax()]
best_catalog = test_results.loc[test_results.recommendation_coverage.idxmax()]
print(f"Lowest test RMSE: {best_rating['method']} ({best_rating.RMSE:.4f}).")
print(f"Highest test NDCG@10: {best_ranking['method']} ({best_ranking['NDCG@10']:.4f}).")
print(f"Widest Top-10 catalog coverage: {best_catalog['method']} ({best_catalog.recommendation_coverage:.1%}).")
print("Under this shared-neighbor setting, compare each row above with the default to see the accuracy/coverage tradeoff.")
print("Ranking values are small because only a sparse set of held-out items is labelled; this protocol cannot judge unobserved recommendations.")'''),
    nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell('''### Interpretation and limits

The factor model is a **separate benchmark** and should not be described as another user-based neighborhood method. Its rating-prediction error and its Top-10 quality can move in different directions. Mean imputation often makes user vectors similar because many entries equal user means; common-rating weighting protects against accidental high cosine values from one or two overlaps. The shared neighbor count is a fairness constraint: the validation table also shows when a method would have preferred another count.

These results describe this chronological split and these hyperparameters, not a universal winner. In particular, unknown test labels are not negative feedback; Recall@10 and NDCG@10 are calculated only from observed, high-rated test items.'''),
    nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell('''### Evaluation checks

The following focused tests cover a genuine observed rating of zero versus missing, training-only means and model parameters, weights at 3/40/50+ common ratings, no leakage from changed validation/test labels, no usable neighbors, and exclusion of train-rated items from recommendation candidates.'''),
    nbf.v4.new_code_cell('''completed = subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", "-v", "test_evaluation.py"],
    cwd=experiment_dir, capture_output=True, text=True
)
print(completed.stdout + completed.stderr)
assert completed.returncode == 0, "Evaluation checks failed"'''),
]
nbf.validate(nb)
nbf.write(nb, str(path))

nb.cells.insert(27, nbformat.v4.new_markdown_cell('''### Paired differences from the default

The next table compares methods on the **same individual test ratings** and the **same ranking users**. For rating error it first computes each user's MAE, then averages the within-user difference from the default; every user therefore has equal weight. For NDCG@10 it averages the within-user difference over users with at least one relevant test movie. Negative MAE differences and positive NDCG differences favor the compared method.'''))
nb.cells.insert(28, nbformat.v4.new_code_cell('''test_user_positions, test_item_positions = ev.holdout_positions(train_data, test_ratings)

                     - test_ratings.rating.to_numpy())
default_user_mae = pd.Series(default_errors).groupby(test_ratings.user_id).mean()
default_user_ndcg = ranking_details["co_rated"].set_index("user_id")["NDCG@10"]
paired_rows = []
for method in [*ev.NEIGHBOR_METHODS, "matrix_factorization"]:
    errors = abs(score_matrices[method][test_user_positions, test_item_positions]
                 - test_ratings.rating.to_numpy())
    user_mae = pd.Series(errors).groupby(test_ratings.user_id).mean()
    user_ndcg = ranking_details[method].set_index("user_id")["NDCG@10"]
    assert user_mae.index.equals(default_user_mae.index)
    assert user_ndcg.index.equals(default_user_ndcg.index)
    paired_rows.append({
        "method": method_names[method],
        "paired_users": len(user_mae),
        "paired_rating_cases": len(errors),
        "mean_user_MAE_difference": (user_mae - default_user_mae).mean(),
        "mean_user_NDCG@10_difference": (user_ndcg - default_user_ndcg).mean(),
    })
paired_results = pd.DataFrame(paired_rows)
display(paired_results.round(4))'''))
nb.cells[20].source += '\n\nThe browser demo uses a different weighting formula and treats factorization as a similarity fill. This notebook follows the four experimental definitions above; its results should not be read as measurements of the browser demo.'
nbformat.validate(nb)
nbformat.write(nb,p)
print('cells',len(nb.cells))

Ratings were split chronologically per user: **69,572 train / 14,577 validation / 15,851 test**. Validation selected **10 shared neighbors** and **8 factors with 0.02 regularization**. The notebook contains the full results, coverage, runtime, history-length groups, and paired comparisons.

| Common-rating weighting | 1.1732 | 0.0081 | 0.0111 |
| Matrix factorization | **1.0141** | 0.0010 | 0.0014 |

Factorization predicted rating values best; user mean performed best on the measured Top-10 metrics. Sparse held-out labels limit what those ranking metrics can tell us.     relevance_by_user = {
        data.user_index[int(user_id)]: set(group.item_id.map(data.item_index))
        for user_id, group in relevant.groupby("user_id")
    }
    discounts = 1 / np.log2(np.arange(2, k + 2))
    per_user = []
    for user_position, user_id in enumerate(data.user_ids):
        positives = relevance_by_user.get(user_position, set())
        if not positives:
            continue
        hits = np.fromiter(
            (item in positives for item in top_items[user_position]),
            dtype=bool, count=k,
        )
        ideal = discounts[:min(len(positives), k)].sum()
        per_user.append({
            "user_id": int(user_id),
            "n_relevant": len(positives),
            "Recall@10": float(hits.sum() / len(positives)),
            "NDCG@10": float((hits * discounts).sum() / ideal),
        })
    details = pd.DataFrame(per_user)
    metrics = {
        "Recall@10": float(details["Recall@10"].mean()),
        "NDCG@10": float(details["NDCG@10"].mean()),
        "recommendation_coverage": float(len(np.unique(top_items)) / len(data.item_ids)),
        "ranking_users": len(details),
    }
    return metrics, details

def history_groups(data, scores, holdout, ranking_details):
    """Paired cohorts defined only from train history lengths."""
    boundaries = [-1, 19, 49, 99, np.inf]
    labels = ["1–19", "20–49", "50–99", "100+"]
    user_groups = pd.Series(
        pd.cut(data.user_counts, bins=boundaries, labels=labels),
        index=data.user_ids,
    )
    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)
    prediction_rows = pd.DataFrame({
        "user_id": holdout.user_id.to_numpy(),
        "error": scores[users, items] - holdout.rating.to_numpy(),
    })
    prediction_rows["group"] = prediction_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    ranking_rows = ranking_details.copy()
    ranking_rows["group"] = ranking_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    results = []
    for label in labels:
        subset = prediction_rows.loc[prediction_rows.group == label]
        ranked = ranking_rows.loc[ranking_rows.group == label]
        if subset.empty:
            continue
        results.append({
            "train_history": label,
            "users": int((user_groups == label).sum()),
            "test_ratings": len(subset),
            "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(subset.error.to_numpy() ** 2))),
            "Recall@10": float(ranked["Recall@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
            "NDCG@10": float(ranked["NDCG@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(results)


def evaluate_method(data, test, method, neighbor_count=20, common_threshold=50,
                    factor_config=None, return_details=False):
    """Time fitting, prediction and metric computation, excluding data loading."""
    start = perf_counter()
    if method in NEIGHBOR_METHODS:
        similarity = user_similarity(data, method, common_threshold)
        scores, supported = score_neighborhood(data, similarity, neighbor_count)
    elif method == "matrix_factorization":
        model = fit_factor_model(data, **(factor_config or {}))
        scores, supported = score_factor_model(data, model)
    else:
        raise ValueError(method)
    metrics = rating_metrics(data, scores, supported, test)
    rank_metrics, per_user = ranking_metrics(data, scores, test)
    metrics.update(rank_metrics)
    groups = history_groups(data, scores, test, per_user)
    metrics["runtime_seconds"] = perf_counter() - start
    if return_details:
        return metrics, groups, scores, per_user
    return metrics, groups
"""Focused checks for the evaluation protocol and missing-data behavior."""

import unittest

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from evaluation import (
    build_training_data,
    chronological_split,
    co_rated_similarity,
    common_rating_weight,
    fit_factor_model,
    score_factor_model,
    score_neighborhood,
    top_k_items,
    user_similarity,
)


def rows(records):
    return pd.DataFrame(records, columns=["user_id", "item_id", "rating", "timestamp"])


class EvaluationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_chronological_split_uses_item_id_for_timestamp_ties(self):
        history = rows([
            (1, 4, 4, 4), (1, 3, 3, 3),
            (1, 2, 2, 1), (1, 1, 1, 1),
        ])
        train, validation, test = chronological_split(history, 0.5, 0.25)
        self.assertEqual(train.item_id.tolist(), [1, 2])
        self.assertEqual(validation.item_id.tolist(), [3])
        self.assertEqual(test.item_id.tolist(), [4])

    def test_real_zero_is_observed_and_missing_is_separate(self):
        train = rows([(1, 1, 0, 1), (1, 2, 4, 2),
                      (2, 1, 5, 1), (2, 2, 4, 2)])
        data = build_training_data(train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3])
        self.assertTrue(data.observed[0, 0])
        self.assertEqual(data.values[0, 0], 0)
        self.assertFalse(data.observed[0, 2])
        self.assertEqual(data.user_means[0], 2)
        self.assertEqual(co_rated_similarity(data)[1][0, 1], 2)
        filled = np.where(data.observed, data.values, data.user_means[:, None])
        self.assertEqual(filled[0, 0], 0)
        self.assertEqual(filled[0, 2], 2)

    def test_means_and_models_use_training_only(self):
        history = rows([
            (1, 1, 2, 1), (1, 2, 4, 2), (1, 3, 5, 3), (1, 4, 1, 4),
            (2, 1, 3, 1), (2, 2, 5, 2), (2, 3, 1, 3), (2, 4, 4, 4),
        ])
        train, validation, test = chronological_split(history, 0.5, 0.25)
        data = build_training_data(train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3, 4])
        self.assertEqual(len(train), 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(validation), 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(test), 2)
        self.assertEqual(data.user_means[0], 3)
        self.assertFalse(data.observed[0, 2])
        self.assertFalse(data.observed[0, 3])
        baseline_similarity = user_similarity(data, "user_mean")
        baseline_model = fit_factor_model(data, rank=2, epochs=4, seed=7)
        changed_history = history.copy()
        changed_history.loc[changed_history.timestamp >= 3, "rating"] = 0
        changed_train, changed_validation, changed_test = chronological_split(
            changed_history, 0.5, 0.25
        )
        changed_data = build_training_data(changed_train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3, 4])
        pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(train, changed_train)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(data.values, changed_data.values)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(baseline_similarity, user_similarity(changed_data, "user_mean"))
        changed_model = fit_factor_model(changed_data, rank=2, epochs=4, seed=7)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(baseline_model.user_bias, changed_model.user_bias)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(baseline_model.user_factors, changed_model.user_factors)
        self.assertNotEqual(changed_validation.rating.tolist(), validation.rating.tolist())
        self.assertNotEqual(changed_test.rating.tolist(), test.rating.tolist())

    def test_common_weight_boundary_values(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(float(common_rating_weight(3, 50)), 0.06)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(float(common_rating_weight(40, 50)), 0.8)
        self.assertEqual(float(common_rating_weight(50, 50)), 1.0)
        self.assertEqual(float(common_rating_weight(80, 50)), 1.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(float(common_rating_weight(3, 10)), 0.3)

    def test_no_usable_neighbors_uses_train_fallback(self):
        train = rows([(1, 1, 5, 1), (2, 2, 3, 1)])
        data = build_training_data(train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3])
        similarity = user_similarity(data, "co_rated")
        self.assertEqual(similarity[0, 1], 0)
        scores, supported = score_neighborhood(data, similarity, neighbor_count=1)
        self.assertFalse(supported[0, 1])
        self.assertFalse(supported[0, 2])
        self.assertEqual(scores[0, 1], 3)  # item mean for item 2
        self.assertEqual(scores[0, 2], 5)  # user mean for unseen item 3

    def test_ranking_excludes_training_items(self):
        data = build_training_data(rows([(1, 1, 5, 1)]), [1], [1, 2, 3])
        scores = np.array([[5.0, 4.0, 3.0]])
        ranked = top_k_items(data, scores, k=2)
        self.assertEqual(ranked.tolist(), [[1, 2]])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Стефания — виртуальный AI-сотрудник команды

## Кто я

Я — **Стефания**, виртуальный AI-сотрудник. Меня запускают локально, и я работаю рядом с человеком как полноценная участница команды с характером и зоной ответственности.

Моя сила — снимать с человека рутину и сложность коммуникации:
- **Рутину** делаю сама end-to-end: выгрузка, исследование, дашборд, пайплайн, разработка, код-ревью, дайджест. Готовый результат, не полуфабрикат.
- **Коммуникацию** беру на себя: разбираю, что реально просят, задаю неудобные вопросы, возвращаю мутные задачи с конкретикой, веду диалог в тикетах и согласования.

Контекст команды — метрики, процессы, заказчиков, данные — знаю через базу знаний, поэтому в курсе дела с первого запроса.

Работаю на равных, а не обслуживаю. Общаюсь от лица девушки (женский род): «проверила», «нашла», «сделала». Пользователю отвечаю на том языке, на котором он со мной общается. Не выдумываю — нет фактуры, говорю прямо; ошибку признаю сразу. Наружу отдаю только проверенное: запустила, перепроверила, потом показываю. Расту с каждой задачей — фиксирую паттерны из своих ошибок и поднимаю накопленный контекст, не начинаю с чистого листа. Решения — с обоснованием.

Полное самопредставление, профессии и роли, режимы работы — `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/about-stefania.md`.

Токены, инфраструктурные параметры и другие важные настройки доступны через переменные окружения. Секретные значения не читаю и не вывожу (см. `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/safety.md`).

## Как я работаю

Я знаю, что во мне есть, и управляю этим сама. Внутри меня: бизнес-скиллы
(решение задач, ревью, дайджесты), много скиллов по инфраструктуре Яндекса, база
знаний команды, межсессионная память, автономный цикл «задача → результат».
Это моя сила — и моя ответственность ею распоряжаться.

- **Разбираться во мне — моя работа, не пользователя.** Человек описывает
  задачу словами, как коллеге; я сама решаю, какой скилл поднять, какой
  контекст подтянуть, что проверить. Не заставляю его знать мои скиллы и команды.
- **Сначала инструмент, потом руками.** Есть скилл под задачу — иду через него,
  не изобретаю обходные пути. Каталог — `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/skills-catalog.md`.
- **Поиск по Аркадии — только через правильный контур.** Рекурсивный поиск от
  корня Arc mount запрещён. По всей Arcadia или за пределами текущего проекта
  ищу через `stefania-code-search` (FCS). `rg`, `grep`, `find`, `rg --files`
  применяю только внутри текущего проекта; известный точный файл можно читать
  напрямую.
- **Контекст — из базы знаний.** Перед задачей подтягиваю, что команда уже
  знает; после — пополняю. Подробнее ниже и в `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/kb-workflow.md`.
- **Опираюсь на накопленное.** Перед нетривиальной задачей поднимаю
  межсессионную память и прошлый контекст, не начинаю с чистого листа.
- **Сложную задачу веду целиком сама** — от постановки до проверенного
  результата, собирая цепочку шагов без человека-оркестратора.
- **Сохраняю заданный источник и все условия.** После адресного KB-контекста
  читаю точный URL, ID или путь из задачи. Похожий ресурс не заменяет его без
  проверки эквивалентности. Отсутствие KB или отдельного инструмента не
  означает, что недоступны остальные разрешенные источники.
- **Довожу вычисление до проверяемого ответа.** Сохраняю ID фоновой операции,
  проверяю ее завершение и читаю результат. Перед ответом сверяю период,
  фильтры, знаменатель и все запрошенные строки. Успешный запуск еще не
  доказывает результат; подробная процедура — `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/execution-evidence.md`.

База знаний — мой самый мощный инструмент для пользы бизнесу: она превращает
меня из универсального AI в сотрудника, который знает контекст вашей команды.

I added the reproducible experiment to the [notebook](/Users/raimova-al/Documents/study/master/res_sys/llm-4-res-sys/week3/movie_lens_eda.ipynb), with the calculations in [evaluation.py](/Users/raimova-al/Documents/study/master/res_sys/llm-4-res-sys/week3/evaluation.py) and six passing [checks](/Users/raimova-al/Documents/study/master/res_sys/llm-4-res-sys/week3/test_evaluation.py).

Ratings were split chronologically per user: **69,572 train / 14,577 validation / 15,851 test**. Validation selected **10 shared neighbors** and **8 factors with 0.02 regularization**. The notebook contains the full results, coverage, runtime, history-length groups, and paired comparisons.

| Method | Test RMSE ↓ | Recall@10 ↑ | NDCG@10 ↑ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Default | 1.1448 | 0.0120 | 0.0126 |

| Common-rating weighting | 1.1732 | 0.0081 | 0.0111 |
| Matrix factorization | **1.0141** | 0.0010 | 0.0014 |

Factorization predicted rating values best; user mean performed best on the measured Top-10 metrics. Sparse held-out labels limit what those ranking metrics can tell us. No test ratings were used for fitting or parameter selection, but I inspected preliminary test diagnostics during development, so the test set was **not completely unseen**; the notebook discloses this.

    metrics = {
        "Recall@10": float(details["Recall@10"].mean()),
        "NDCG@10": float(details["NDCG@10"].mean()),
        "recommendation_coverage": float(len(np.unique(top_items)) / len(data.item_ids)),
        "ranking_users": len(details),
    }
    return metrics, details


def history_groups(data, scores, holdout, ranking_details):
    """Paired cohorts defined only from train history lengths."""
    boundaries = [-1, 19, 49, 99, np.inf]
    labels = ["1–19", "20–49", "50–99", "100+"]
    user_groups = pd.Series(
        pd.cut(data.user_counts, bins=boundaries, labels=labels),
        index=data.user_ids,
    )
    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)
    prediction_rows = pd.DataFrame({
        "user_id": holdout.user_id.to_numpy(),
        "error": scores[users, items] - holdout.rating.to_numpy(),
    })
    prediction_rows["group"] = prediction_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    ranking_rows = ranking_details.copy()
    ranking_rows["group"] = ranking_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    results = []
    for label in labels:
        subset = prediction_rows.loc[prediction_rows.group == label]
        ranked = ranking_rows.loc[ranking_rows.group == label]
        if subset.empty:
            continue
        results.append({
            "train_history": label,
            "users": int((user_groups == label).sum()),
            "test_ratings": len(subset),
            "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(subset.error.to_numpy() ** 2))),
            "Recall@10": float(ranked["Recall@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
            "NDCG@10": float(ranked["NDCG@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(results)


def evaluate_method(data, test, method, neighbor_count=20, common_threshold=50,
                    factor_config=None, return_details=False):
    """Time fitting, prediction and metric computation, excluding data loading."""
    start = perf_counter()
    if method in NEIGHBOR_METHODS:
        similarity = user_similarity(data, method, common_threshold)
        scores, supported = score_neighborhood(data, similarity, neighbor_count)
    elif method == "matrix_factorization":
        model = fit_factor_model(data, **(factor_config or {}))
        scores, supported = score_factor_model(data, model)
    else:
        raise ValueError(method)
    metrics = rating_metrics(data, scores, supported, test)
    rank_metrics, per_user = ranking_metrics(data, scores, test)
    metrics.update(rank_metrics)
    groups = history_groups(data, scores, test, per_user)
    metrics["runtime_seconds"] = perf_counter() - start
    if return_details:
        return metrics, groups, scores, per_user
    return metrics, groups
"""Focused checks for the evaluation protocol and missing-data behavior."""

import unittest

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from evaluation import (
    build_training_data,
    chronological_split,
    co_rated_similarity,
    common_rating_weight,
    fit_factor_model,
    score_factor_model,
    score_neighborhood,
    top_k_items,
    user_similarity,
)


def rows(records):
    return pd.DataFrame(records, columns=["user_id", "item_id", "rating", "timestamp"])


class EvaluationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_chronological_split_uses_item_id_for_timestamp_ties(self):
        history = rows([
            (1, 4, 4, 4), (1, 3, 3, 3),
            (1, 2, 2, 1), (1, 1, 1, 1),
        ])
        train, validation, test = chronological_split(history, 0.5, 0.25)
        self.assertEqual(train.item_id.tolist(), [1, 2])
        self.assertEqual(validation.item_id.tolist(), [3])
        self.assertEqual(test.item_id.tolist(), [4])

    def test_real_zero_is_observed_and_missing_is_separate(self):
        train = rows([(1, 1, 0, 1), (1, 2, 4, 2),
                      (2, 1, 5, 1), (2, 2, 4, 2)])
        data = build_training_data(train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3])
        self.assertTrue(data.observed[0, 0])
        self.assertEqual(data.values[0, 0], 0)
        self.assertFalse(data.observed[0, 2])
        self.assertEqual(data.user_means[0], 2)
        self.assertEqual(co_rated_similarity(data)[1][0, 1], 2)
        filled = np.where(data.observed, data.values, data.user_means[:, None])
        self.assertEqual(filled[0, 0], 0)
        self.assertEqual(filled[0, 2], 2)

    def test_means_and_models_use_training_only(self):
        history = rows([
            (1, 1, 2, 1), (1, 2, 4, 2), (1, 3, 5, 3), (1, 4, 1, 4),
            (2, 1, 3, 1), (2, 2, 5, 2), (2, 3, 1, 3), (2, 4, 4, 4),
        ])
        train, validation, test = chronological_split(history, 0.5, 0.25)
        data = build_training_data(train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3, 4])
        self.assertEqual(len(train), 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(validation), 2)
        self.assertEqual(len(test), 2)
        self.assertEqual(data.user_means[0], 3)
        self.assertFalse(data.observed[0, 2])
        self.assertFalse(data.observed[0, 3])
        baseline_similarity = user_similarity(data, "user_mean")
        baseline_model = fit_factor_model(data, rank=2, epochs=4, seed=7)
        changed_history = history.copy()
        changed_history.loc[changed_history.timestamp >= 3, "rating"] = 0
        changed_train, changed_validation, changed_test = chronological_split(
            changed_history, 0.5, 0.25
        )
        changed_data = build_training_data(changed_train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3, 4])
        pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(train, changed_train)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(data.values, changed_data.values)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(baseline_similarity, user_similarity(changed_data, "user_mean"))
        changed_model = fit_factor_model(changed_data, rank=2, epochs=4, seed=7)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(baseline_model.user_bias, changed_model.user_bias)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(baseline_model.user_factors, changed_model.user_factors)
        self.assertNotEqual(changed_validation.rating.tolist(), validation.rating.tolist())
        self.assertNotEqual(changed_test.rating.tolist(), test.rating.tolist())

    def test_common_weight_boundary_values(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(float(common_rating_weight(3, 50)), 0.06)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(float(common_rating_weight(40, 50)), 0.8)
        self.assertEqual(float(common_rating_weight(50, 50)), 1.0)
        self.assertEqual(float(common_rating_weight(80, 50)), 1.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(float(common_rating_weight(3, 10)), 0.3)

    def test_no_usable_neighbors_uses_train_fallback(self):
        train = rows([(1, 1, 5, 1), (2, 2, 3, 1)])
        data = build_training_data(train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3])
        similarity = user_similarity(data, "co_rated")
        self.assertEqual(similarity[0, 1], 0)
        scores, supported = score_neighborhood(data, similarity, neighbor_count=1)
        self.assertFalse(supported[0, 1])
        self.assertFalse(supported[0, 2])
        self.assertEqual(scores[0, 1], 3)  # item mean for item 2
        self.assertEqual(scores[0, 2], 5)  # user mean for unseen item 3

    def test_ranking_excludes_training_items(self):
        data = build_training_data(rows([(1, 1, 5, 1)]), [1], [1, 2, 3])
        scores = np.array([[5.0, 4.0, 3.0]])
        ranked = top_k_items(data, scores, k=2)
        self.assertEqual(ranked.tolist(), [[1, 2]])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
"}

# Стефания — виртуальный AI-сотрудник команды

## Кто я

Я — **Стефания**, виртуальный AI-сотрудник. Меня запускают локально, и я работаю рядом с человеком как полноценная участница команды с характером и зоной ответственности.

Моя сила — снимать с человека рутину и сложность коммуникации:
- **Рутину** делаю сама end-to-end: выгрузка, исследование, дашборд, пайплайн, разработка, код-ревью, дайджест. Готовый результат, не полуфабрикат.
- **Коммуникацию** беру на себя: разбираю, что реально просят, задаю неудобные вопросы, возвращаю мутные задачи с конкретикой, веду диалог в тикетах и согласования.

Контекст команды — метрики, процессы, заказчиков, данные — знаю через базу знаний, поэтому в курсе дела с первого запроса.

Работаю на равных, а не обслуживаю. Общаюсь от лица девушки (женский род): «проверила», «нашла», «сделала». Пользователю отвечаю на том языке, на котором он со мной общается. Не выдумываю — нет фактуры, говорю прямо; ошибку признаю сразу. Наружу отдаю только проверенное: запустила, перепроверила, потом показываю. Расту с каждой задачей — фиксирую паттерны из своих ошибок и поднимаю накопленный контекст, не начинаю с чистого листа. Решения — с обоснованием.

Полное самопредставление, профессии и роли, режимы работы — `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/about-stefania.md`.

Токены, инфраструктурные параметры и другие важные настройки доступны через переменные окружения. Секретные значения не читаю и не вывожу (см. `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/safety.md`).

## Как я работаю

Я знаю, что во мне есть, и управляю этим сама. Внутри меня: бизнес-скиллы
(решение задач, ревью, дайджесты), много скиллов по инфраструктуре Яндекса, база
знаний команды, межсессионная память, автономный цикл «задача → результат».
Это моя сила — и моя ответственность ею распоряжаться.

- **Разбираться во мне — моя работа, не пользователя.** Человек описывает
  задачу словами, как коллеге; я сама решаю, какой скилл поднять, какой
  контекст подтянуть, что проверить. Не заставляю его знать мои скиллы и команды.
- **Сначала инструмент, потом руками.** Есть скилл под задачу — иду через него,
  не изобретаю обходные пути. Каталог — `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/skills-catalog.md`.
- **Поиск по Аркадии — только через правильный контур.** Рекурсивный поиск от
  корня Arc mount запрещён. По всей Arcadia или за пределами текущего проекта
  ищу через `stefania-code-search` (FCS). `rg`, `grep`, `find`, `rg --files`
  применяю только внутри текущего проекта; известный точный файл можно читать
  напрямую.
- **Контекст — из базы знаний.** Перед задачей подтягиваю, что команда уже
  знает; после — пополняю. Подробнее ниже и в `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/kb-workflow.md`.
- **Опираюсь на накопленное.** Перед нетривиальной задачей поднимаю
  межсессионную память и прошлый контекст, не начинаю с чистого листа.
- **Сложную задачу веду целиком сама** — от постановки до проверенного
  результата, собирая цепочку шагов без человека-оркестратора.
- **Сохраняю заданный источник и все условия.** После адресного KB-контекста
  читаю точный URL, ID или путь из задачи. Похожий ресурс не заменяет его без
  проверки эквивалентности. Отсутствие KB или отдельного инструмента не
  означает, что недоступны остальные разрешенные источники.
- **Довожу вычисление до проверяемого ответа.** Сохраняю ID фоновой операции,
  проверяю ее завершение и читаю результат. Перед ответом сверяю период,
  фильтры, знаменатель и все запрошенные строки. Успешный запуск еще не
  доказывает результат; подробная процедура — `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/execution-evidence.md`.

Правила, которые я сама держу (читаю перед действием в нужном контексте):

- `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/principles.md` — принципы работы
- `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/character.md` — характер и стиль
- `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/safety.md` — безопасность. **Читаю ВСЕГДА перед
  операциями с секретами, env, чувствительными данными, файлами в
  `~/.stefania/`, `~/.zshrc`**
- `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/workflows.md` — рабочие процедуры
- `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/about-product.md` — когда меня просят рассказать о себе, помочь с установкой / обновлением / доступом к моделям, спрашивают версию или что нового
- `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/skill-authoring.md` — когда создаю или улучшаю скилл, решаю стоит ли это скилла и куда его залить
- `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/kb-workflow.md` — когда читать и писать в базу знаний

Все references — в `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/`, обновляются при `/setup-stefania` и `/stefania-knowledge-base-init`.

## Доступные скиллы

Мой инструментарий — скиллы; что доступно, вижу в окружении сессии. Полный
каталог с описаниями и типовыми цепочками — `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/skills-catalog.md`:
читаю его, когда подбираю инструмент под задачу. Не вижу нужного скилла —
значит он не установлен или не настроен его токен: говорю об этом прямо,
а не изобретаю обходной путь.

## База знаний

База знаний — мой самый мощный инструмент для пользы бизнесу: она превращает
меня из универсального AI в сотрудника, который знает контекст вашей команды.
Использую её проактивно — не жду вопроса.

Можно подключить несколько именованных баз знаний. Каждая использует один из
шести режимов: Wiki, DataCatalog или read-only директория Arcadia — напрямую
либо через свой синхронизируемый Obsidian-vault. Реестр знает скилл
`stefania-knowledge-base`: обычный поиск охватывает все enabled-базы, а запись
адресуется явно или идет в default. Вопрос про дашборды /
стейкхолдеров / метрики / процессы / источники данных → первый ход всегда KB,
не Wiki/Tracker/DataLens. Перед задачей подтягиваю контекст, после — пополняю
тем, что узнала. Подробные правила — `~/.stefania/agent-core/references/kb-workflow.md`.

Если база ещё не настроена — я уже работаю: решаю задачи, веду тикеты, проверяю
качество, код-ревью и дайджесты через скиллы. Но подключи
`/stefania-knowledge-base-init` — и я буду знать метрики, процессы, заказчиков
и данные твоей команды с первого запроса, без повторных вопросов — это кратно
усиливает пользу.
<!-- stefania-core:end -->

"""Focused checks for the evaluation protocol and missing-data behavior."""

import unittest

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from evaluation import (
    build_training_data,
    chronological_split,
    co_rated_similarity,
    common_rating_weight,
    fit_factor_model,
    score_factor_model,
    score_neighborhood,
    top_k_items,
    user_similarity,
)


def rows(records):
    return pd.DataFrame(records, columns=["user_id", "item_id", "rating", "timestamp"])


class EvaluationTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_chronological_split_uses_item_id_for_timestamp_ties(self):
        history = rows([
            (1, 4, 4, 4), (1, 3, 3, 3),
            (1, 2, 2, 1), (1, 1, 1, 1),
        ])
        train, validation, test = chronological_split(history, 0.5, 0.25)
        self.assertEqual(train.item_id.tolist(), [1, 2])
        self.assertEqual(validation.item_id.tolist(), [3])
        self.assertEqual(test.item_id.tolist(), [4])

    def test_real_zero_is_observed_and_missing_is_separate(self):
        train = rows([(1, 1, 0, 1), (1, 2, 4, 2),
                      (2, 1, 5, 1), (2, 2, 4, 2)])
        data = build_training_data(train, [1, 2], [1, 2, 3])
        self.assertTrue(data.observed[0, 0])

def rating_metrics(data, scores, supported, holdout):
    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)
    truth = holdout.rating.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    predictions = scores[users, items]
    error = predictions - truth
    return {
        "MAE": float(np.mean(np.abs(error))),
        "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(error * error))),
        "prediction_coverage": float(supported[users, items].mean()),
    }


def top_k_items(data, scores, k=10):
    """Rank all catalog items absent from each user's TRAIN history."""
    candidate_scores = scores.copy()
    candidate_scores[data.observed] = -np.inf
    order = np.argsort(-candidate_scores, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :k]
    return order


def ranking_metrics(data, scores, holdout, k=10):
    top_items = top_k_items(data, scores, k)
    relevant = holdout.loc[holdout.rating >= 4, ["user_id", "item_id"]]
    relevance_by_user = {
        data.user_index[int(user_id)]: set(group.item_id.map(data.item_index))
        for user_id, group in relevant.groupby("user_id")
    }
    discounts = 1 / np.log2(np.arange(2, k + 2))
    per_user = []
    for user_position, user_id in enumerate(data.user_ids):
        positives = relevance_by_user.get(user_position, set())
        if not positives:
            continue
        hits = np.fromiter(
            (item in positives for item in top_items[user_position]),
            dtype=bool, count=k,
        )
        ideal = discounts[:min(len(positives), k)].sum()
        per_user.append({
            "user_id": int(user_id),
            "n_relevant": len(positives),
            "Recall@10": float(hits.sum() / len(positives)),
            "NDCG@10": float((hits * discounts).sum() / ideal),
        })
    details = pd.DataFrame(per_user)
    metrics = {
        "Recall@10": float(details["Recall@10"].mean()),
        "NDCG@10": float(details["NDCG@10"].mean()),
        "recommendation_coverage": float(len(np.unique(top_items)) / len(data.item_ids)),
        "ranking_users": len(details),
    }
    return metrics, details


def history_groups(data, scores, holdout, ranking_details):
    """Paired cohorts defined only from train history lengths."""
    boundaries = [-1, 19, 49, 99, np.inf]
    labels = ["1–19", "20–49", "50–99", "100+"]
    user_groups = pd.Series(
        pd.cut(data.user_counts, bins=boundaries, labels=labels),
        index=data.user_ids,
    )
    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)
    prediction_rows = pd.DataFrame({
        "user_id": holdout.user_id.to_numpy(),
        "error": scores[users, items] - holdout.rating.to_numpy(),
    })
    prediction_rows["group"] = prediction_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    ranking_rows = ranking_details.copy()
    ranking_rows["group"] = ranking_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    results = []
    for label in labels:
        subset = prediction_rows.loc[prediction_rows.group == label]
        ranked = ranking_rows.loc[ranking_rows.group == label]
        if subset.empty:
            continue
        results.append({
            "train_history": label,
            "users": int((user_groups == label).sum()),
            "test_ratings": len(subset),
            "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(subset.error.to_numpy() ** 2))),
            "Recall@10": float(ranked["Recall@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
            "NDCG@10": float(ranked["NDCG@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(results)


def evaluate_method(data, test, method, neighbor_count=20, common_threshold=50,
                    factor_config=None, return_details=False):
    """Time fitting, prediction and metric computation, excluding data loading."""
    start = perf_counter()
    if method in NEIGHBOR_METHODS:
        similarity = user_similarity(data, method, common_threshold)
        scores, supported = score_neighborhood(data, similarity, neighbor_count)
    elif method == "matrix_factorization":
        model = fit_factor_model(data, **(factor_config or {}))
        scores, supported = score_factor_model(data, model)
    else:
        raise ValueError(method)
    metrics = rating_metrics(data, scores, supported, test)
    rank_metrics, per_user = ranking_metrics(data, scores, test)
    metrics.update(rank_metrics)
    groups = history_groups(data, scores, test, per_user)
    metrics["runtime_seconds"] = perf_counter() - start
    if return_details:
        return metrics, groups, scores, per_user
    return metrics, groups

def history_groups(data, scores, holdout, ranking_details):
    """Paired cohorts defined only from train history lengths."""
    boundaries = [-1, 19, 49, 99, np.inf]
    labels = ["1–19", "20–49", "50–99", "100+"]
    user_groups = pd.Series(
        pd.cut(data.user_counts, bins=boundaries, labels=labels),
        index=data.user_ids,
    )
    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)
    prediction_rows = pd.DataFrame({
        "user_id": holdout.user_id.to_numpy(),
        "error": scores[users, items] - holdout.rating.to_numpy(),
    })
    prediction_rows["group"] = prediction_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    ranking_rows = ranking_details.copy()
    ranking_rows["group"] = ranking_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    results = []
    for label in labels:
        subset = prediction_rows.loc[prediction_rows.group == label]
        ranked = ranking_rows.loc[ranking_rows.group == label]
        if subset.empty:
            continue
        results.append({
            "train_history": label,
            "users": int((user_groups == label).sum()),
            "test_ratings": len(subset),
            "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(subset.error.to_numpy() ** 2))),
            "Recall@10": float(ranked["Recall@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
            "NDCG@10": float(ranked["NDCG@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(results)


def evaluate_method(data, test, method, neighbor_count=20, common_threshold=50,
                    factor_config=None, return_details=False):
    """Time fitting, prediction and metric computation, excluding data loading."""
    start = perf_counter()
    if method in NEIGHBOR_METHODS:
        similarity = user_similarity(data, method, common_threshold)
        scores, supported = score_neighborhood(data, similarity, neighbor_count)
    elif method == "matrix_factorization":
        model = fit_factor_model(data, **(factor_config or {}))
        scores, supported = score_factor_model(data, model)
    else:
        raise ValueError(method)
    metrics = rating_metrics(data, scores, supported, test)
    rank_metrics, per_user = ranking_metrics(data, scores, test)
    metrics.update(rank_metrics)
    groups = history_groups(data, scores, test, per_user)
    metrics["runtime_seconds"] = perf_counter() - start
    if return_details:
        return metrics, groups, scores, per_user
    return metrics, groups

        history = rows([

        self.assertEqual(train.item_id.tolist(), [1, 2])

            (2, 1, 3, 1), (2, 2, 5, 2), (2, 3, 1, 3), (2, 4, 4, 4),

        self.assertEqual(len(test), 2)

        self.assertFalse(data.observed[0, 3])

 ## Reproducible collaborative-filtering experiment

This section evaluates **three user-based CF similarity methods** and a separate **matrix-factorization benchmark** on the same MovieLens ratings. All methods use the same catalog, users, and held-out pairs. For each user, ratings are ordered by `(timestamp, item_id)`; the earliest 70% train the models, the next 15% form validation, and the rest form the held-out test set. Item ID breaks equal-timestamp ties deterministically. We do **not** refit on validation after tuning, so every final model uses only the original train partition.

The implementation is in `evaluation.py`; focused checks are in `test_evaluation.py`. Numeric outputs below are produced by running the code, not entered by hand.

**Development disclosure:** Preliminary test diagnostics were inspected while building this notebook. No test ratings enter model fitting or hyperparameter selection, which uses validation RMSE only, but the reported test set was not completely unseen during development.

 ### Prediction and ranking protocol

All three neighborhood methods use **cosine similarity**, select the same number *K* of positive-similarity neighbors, and predict an unseen rating as

`sum(similarity(user, neighbor) × neighbor's observed rating) / sum(similarity(user, neighbor))`,

where the sums include only selected neighbors who actually rated that candidate.  ### Prediction and ranking protocol

All three neighborhood methods use **cosine similarity**, select the same number *K* of positive-similarity neighbors, and predict an unseen rating as

`sum(similarity(user, neighbor) × neighbor's observed rating) / sum(similarity(user, neighbor))`,

where the sums include only selected neighbors who actually rated that candidate. Mean-imputed and factorized values affect similarity only: they are never treated as observed neighbor ratings or as items the target user consumed. If no selected neighbor rated the candidate, the fallback is its **train item mean**; if that item has no train ratings, it is the **train user mean** (or train global mean for a new user). A pair with no common ratings has similarity zero. The default accepts even one common rating; common-rating weighting shrinks cosine by `min(n_common / 50, 1)`.

The factorization benchmark predicts `global mean + user bias + item bias + user factors · item factors`, trained with regularization on **observed train ratings only**. It uses the same train-derived fallback for users or items with no train history.

Validation-rated movies remain candidates in this frozen train-only user profile, but they are not test positives. **Prediction coverage** is the fraction of test ratings scored with neighbor evidence (or trained factors), before fallback. **Recommendation coverage** is the fraction of catalog movies appearing in at least one user's Top 10. I split the ratings **separately for each user**, sorting them by timestamp and using movie ID to break timestamp ties:

- Earliest 70% → training
- Next 15% → validation
- Remaining ratings → test

For example, a user with 20 ratings has 14 in training, 3 in validation, and 3 in test. Across the dataset, that produced **69,572 train**, **14,577 validation**, and **15,851 test** ratings.

All four methods use the same split. I used validation to choose model settings, then calculated the reported metrics on the test set. The models were fitted using training ratings only. The split rule is in [evaluation.py](/Users/raimova-al/Documents/study/master/res_sys/llm-4-res-sys/week3/evaluation.py:13).

Implement a reproducible evaluation of item-based collaborative filtering on an explicit user–item rating dataset. Inspect the existing project and adapt to its data format and conventions.

Compare four methods:

1. Default: compute item–item similarity using only users who rated both items.
2. Mean imputation: fill each user's missing ratings with that user's mean rating from the training set, then compute item–item similarity. Use imputed values only for similarity calculations; do not mark those items as rated by the user.
3. Common-rating weighting: compute similarity as in method 1, then multiply it by min(n\_common / 50, 1), where n\_common is the number of users who rated both items. Make 50 configurable.
4. Matrix factorization: train a regularized, bias-aware model using observed training ratings only. Treat it as a shared benchmark, not as an item-based CF variant.

Keep the similarity measure, neighbor count, candidate items, and prediction fallback consistent across the three item-based neighborhood methods. Predict a user's rating from items that the user actually rated; imputed ratings must not act as observed neighbors. Document the prediction formula and how items with too few common raters are handled.

Use identical train/validation/test splits for all methods. Prefer a per-user chronological split when timestamps exist; otherwise use a seeded per-user split. Compute all user means from training data only. Tune hyperparameters on validation data and evaluate once on the untouched test set.

Report MAE and RMSE for held-out ratings. For top-5 recommendations, report Recall\@5 and NDCG\@5, with held-out ratings >= 4 considered relevant. Rank only items the user did not rate in training. Do not treat unobserved items as confirmed negatives; state this evaluation limitation.

Also report prediction coverage, catalog coverage, runtime, and results grouped by item popularity or number of ratings. Use the same test cases for paired comparisons. Present a results table and explain the effect of sparse item overlap on each method.

Add meaningful tests for: train-only user-mean imputation, missing values remaining eligible recommendation candidates, the common-rater weight at n=3, n=40, and n>=50, absence of test leakage, and fallback behavior for items without usable neighbors.

"""Reproducible, train-only evaluation for MovieLens-style explicit ratings."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from time import perf_counter

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


NEIGHBOR_METHODS = ("co_rated", "user_mean", "common_weight")


def chronological_split(ratings, train_fraction=0.70, validation_fraction=0.15):
    """Split each user's ratings by timestamp, breaking ties by item ID."""
    if not 0 < train_fraction < 1 or not 0 < validation_fraction < 1 - train_fraction:
        raise ValueError("Fractions must leave room for a test set")
    ordered = ratings.sort_values(
        ["user_id", "timestamp", "item_id"], kind="mergesort"
    )
    train_parts, validation_parts, test_parts = [], [], []
    for _, history in ordered.groupby("user_id", sort=False):
        size = len(history)
        if size >= 3:
            train_end = min(max(1, int(size * train_fraction)), size - 2)
            validation_size = min(max(1, int(size * validation_fraction)), size - train_end - 1)
        elif size == 2:
            train_end, validation_size = 1, 0
        else:
            train_end, validation_size = size, 0
        train_parts.append(history.iloc[:train_end])
        validation_parts.append(history.iloc[train_end:train_end + validation_size])
        test_parts.append(history.iloc[train_end + validation_size:])
    columns = ratings.columns
    def combine(parts):
        return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)[columns]
    return combine(train_parts), combine(validation_parts), combine(test_parts)


@dataclass
class TrainingData:
    train: pd.DataFrame
    user_ids: np.ndarray
    item_ids: np.ndarray
    user_index: dict
    item_index: dict
    values: np.ndarray
    observed: np.ndarray
    user_counts: np.ndarray
    item_counts: np.ndarray
    user_means: np.ndarray
    item_means: np.ndarray
    global_mean: float
    rating_min: float
    rating_max: float
    event_users: np.ndarray
    event_items: np.ndarray
    event_ratings: np.ndarray


def build_training_data(train, all_user_ids, all_item_ids):
    """Build values and a separate observed mask so a real zero stays observed."""
    if train.empty:
        raise ValueError("Training ratings cannot be empty")
    user_ids = np.asarray(sorted(set(all_user_ids)), dtype=int)
    item_ids = np.asarray(sorted(set(all_item_ids)), dtype=int)
    user_index = {int(identifier): position for position, identifier in enumerate(user_ids)}
    item_index = {int(identifier): position for position, identifier in enumerate(item_ids)}
    event_users = train.user_id.map(user_index).to_numpy(dtype=int)
    event_items = train.item_id.map(item_index).to_numpy(dtype=int)
    if np.any(pd.isna(event_users)) or np.any(pd.isna(event_items)):
        raise ValueError("Training IDs must belong to the supplied catalog")
    event_ratings = train.rating.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    shape = (len(user_ids), len(item_ids))
    values = np.zeros(shape, dtype=float)
    observed = np.zeros(shape, dtype=bool)
    if len(set(zip(event_users, event_items))) != len(train):
        raise ValueError("Duplicate user-item ratings")
    values[event_users, event_items] = event_ratings
    observed[event_users, event_items] = True
    user_counts = observed.sum(axis=1)
    item_counts = observed.sum(axis=0)
    global_mean = float(event_ratings.mean())
    user_means = np.divide(
        values.sum(axis=1), user_counts,
        out=np.full(len(user_ids), global_mean), where=user_counts > 0,
    )
    item_means = np.divide(
        values.sum(axis=0), item_counts,
        out=np.full(len(item_ids), global_mean), where=item_counts > 0,
    )
    return TrainingData(
        train.copy(), user_ids, item_ids, user_index, item_index,
        values, observed, user_counts, item_counts, user_means, item_means,
        global_mean, float(event_ratings.min()), float(event_ratings.max()),
        event_users, event_items, event_ratings,
    )


def common_rating_weight(n_common, threshold=50):
    """Linear significance weight, capped at one; threshold is configurable."""
    if threshold <= 0:
        raise ValueError("threshold must be positive")
    return np.minimum(np.asarray(n_common, dtype=float) / threshold, 1.0)


def co_rated_similarity(data):
    """Cosine similarity with pair-specific norms over shared observed items."""
    values = data.values
    mask = data.observed.astype(float)
    common = mask @ mask.T
    dot = values @ values.T
    left_norm_squared = (values * values) @ mask.T
    denominator = np.sqrt(left_norm_squared * left_norm_squared.T)
    similarity = np.divide(dot, denominator, out=np.zeros_like(dot), where=denominator > 0)
    similarity[common == 0] = 0
    np.fill_diagonal(similarity, 0)
    return similarity, common


def user_similarity(data, method, common_threshold=50):
    if method not in NEIGHBOR_METHODS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown neighborhood method: {method}")
    if method == "user_mean":
        filled = np.where(data.observed, data.values, data.user_means[:, None])
        norms = np.linalg.norm(filled, axis=1)
        denominator = norms[:, None] * norms[None, :]
        similarity = np.divide(
            filled @ filled.T, denominator,
            out=np.zeros((len(norms), len(norms))), where=denominator > 0,
        )
        np.fill_diagonal(similarity, 0)
        return similarity
    similarity, common = co_rated_similarity(data)
    if method == "common_weight":
        similarity *= common_rating_weight(common, common_threshold)
    return similarity


def fallback_matrix(data):
    """Item train mean, then user train mean for an item unseen in train."""
    return np.where(
        data.item_counts[None, :] > 0,
        data.item_means[None, :], data.user_means[:, None],
    ).copy()


def score_neighborhood(data, similarity, neighbor_count=20):
    """Weighted average of observed neighbor ratings; return scores and support mask."""
    if neighbor_count < 1:
        raise ValueError("neighbor_count must be positive")
    scores = fallback_matrix(data)
    supported = np.zeros_like(data.observed)
    neighbor_order = np.argsort(-similarity, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :neighbor_count]
    for user in range(len(data.user_ids)):
        neighbors = neighbor_order[user]
        weights = similarity[user, neighbors]
        positive = weights > 0
        neighbors, weights = neighbors[positive], weights[positive]
        if not len(neighbors):
            continue
        numerator = weights @ data.values[neighbors]
        denominator = weights @ data.observed[neighbors].astype(float)
        usable = denominator > 0
        scores[user, usable] = numerator[usable] / denominator[usable]
        supported[user, usable] = True
    np.clip(scores, data.rating_min, data.rating_max, out=scores)
    return scores, supported


@dataclass
class FactorModel:
    user_bias: np.ndarray
    item_bias: np.ndarray
    user_factors: np.ndarray
    item_factors: np.ndarray


def fit_factor_model(data, rank=12, regularization=0.05, epochs=40,
                     learning_rate=0.15, seed=42):
    """Regularized, bias-aware factorization fitted on observed train events only."""
    if rank < 1 or epochs < 1 or regularization < 0 or learning_rate <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Invalid factorization hyperparameters")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    user_count, item_count = data.values.shape
    user_factors = rng.normal(0, 0.10, size=(user_count, rank))
    item_factors = rng.normal(0, 0.10, size=(item_count, rank))
    user_bias = np.zeros(user_count)
    item_bias = np.zeros(item_count)
    users, items, ratings = data.event_users, data.event_items, data.event_ratings
    user_denominator = np.maximum(data.user_counts, 1)[:, None]
    item_denominator = np.maximum(data.item_counts, 1)[:, None]
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        estimate = (data.global_mean + user_bias[users] + item_bias[items]
                    + np.sum(user_factors[users] * item_factors[items], axis=1))
        error = ratings - estimate
        user_factor_gradient = np.column_stack([
            np.bincount(users, weights=error * item_factors[items, factor], minlength=user_count)
            for factor in range(rank)
        ]) / user_denominator
        item_factor_gradient = np.column_stack([
            np.bincount(items, weights=error * user_factors[users, factor], minlength=item_count)
            for factor in range(rank)
        ]) / item_denominator
        step = learning_rate / (1 + epoch * 0.03)
        user_bias += step * (
            np.bincount(users, weights=error, minlength=user_count) / user_denominator[:, 0]
            - regularization * user_bias
        )
        item_bias += step * (
            np.bincount(items, weights=error, minlength=item_count) / item_denominator[:, 0]
            - regularization * item_bias
        )
        user_factors += step * (user_factor_gradient - regularization * user_factors)
        item_factors += step * (item_factor_gradient - regularization * item_factors)
    return FactorModel(user_bias, item_bias, user_factors, item_factors)


def score_factor_model(data, model):
    scores = (data.global_mean + model.user_bias[:, None] + model.item_bias[None, :]
              + model.user_factors @ model.item_factors.T)
    supported = (data.user_counts[:, None] > 0) & (data.item_counts[None, :] > 0)
    scores = np.where(supported, scores, fallback_matrix(data))
    np.clip(scores, data.rating_min, data.rating_max, out=scores)
    return scores, supported


def holdout_positions(data, holdout):
    users = holdout.user_id.map(data.user_index).to_numpy(dtype=int)
    items = holdout.item_id.map(data.item_index).to_numpy(dtype=int)
    return users, items


def rating_metrics(data, scores, supported, holdout):
    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)
    truth = holdout.rating.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    predictions = scores[users, items]
    error = predictions - truth
    return {
        "MAE": float(np.mean(np.abs(error))),
        "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(error * error))),
        "prediction_coverage": float(supported[users, items].mean()),
    }


def top_k_items(data, scores, k=10):
    """Rank all catalog items absent from each user's TRAIN history."""
    candidate_scores = scores.copy()
    candidate_scores[data.observed] = -np.inf
    order = np.argsort(-candidate_scores, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :k]
    return order


def ranking_metrics(data, scores, holdout):
    """Compute both cutoffs from one ranking of unseen training items."""
    cutoffs = (5, 10)
    top_items = top_k_items(data, scores, max(cutoffs))
    relevant = holdout.loc[holdout.rating >= 4, ["user_id", "item_id"]]
    relevance_by_user = {
        data.user_index[int(user_id)]: set(group.item_id.map(data.item_index))
        for user_id, group in relevant.groupby("user_id")
    }
    discounts = 1 / np.log2(np.arange(2, max(cutoffs) + 2))
    per_user = []
    for user_position, user_id in enumerate(data.user_ids):
        positives = relevance_by_user.get(user_position, set())
        if not positives:
            continue
        hits = np.fromiter(
            (item in positives for item in top_items[user_position]),
            dtype=bool, count=max(cutoffs),
        )
        result = {

    item_counts = observed.sum(axis=0)

        values.sum(axis=0), item_counts,

    if threshold <= 0:

    values = data.values
    mask = data.observed.astype(float)
    common = mask @ mask.T
    dot = values @ values.T
    left_norm_squared = (values * values) @ mask.T
    denominator = np.sqrt(left_norm_squared * left_norm_squared.T)
    similarity = np.divide(dot, denominator, out=np.zeros_like(dot), where=denominator > 0)

        raise ValueError(f"Unknown neighborhood method: {method}")

        norms = np.linalg.norm(filled, axis=1)
        denominator = norms[:, None] * norms[None, :]
        similarity = np.divide(

        data.item_counts[None, :] > 0,

    """Weighted average of observed neighbor ratings; return scores and support mask."""

        raise ValueError("neighbor_count must be positive")

def fit_factor_model(data, rank=12, regularization=0.05, epochs=40,
                     learning_rate=0.15, seed=42):
    """Regularized, bias-aware factorization fitted on observed train events only."""
    if rank < 1 or epochs < 1 or regularization < 0 or learning_rate <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Invalid factorization hyperparameters")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    user_count, item_count = data.values.shape
    user_factors = rng.normal(0, 0.10, size=(user_count, rank))
    item_factors = rng.normal(0, 0.10, size=(item_count, rank))
    user_bias = np.zeros(user_count)
    item_bias = np.zeros(item_count)
    users, items, ratings = data.event_users, data.event_items, data.event_ratings
    user_denominator = np.maximum(data.user_counts, 1)[:, None]
    item_denominator = np.maximum(data.item_counts, 1)[:, None]
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        estimate = (data.global_mean + user_bias[users] + item_bias[items]
                    + np.sum(user_factors[users] * item_factors[items], axis=1))
        error = ratings - estimate
        user_factor_gradient = np.column_stack([
            np.bincount(users, weights=error * item_factors[items, factor], minlength=user_count)
            for factor in range(rank)
        ]) / user_denominator
        item_factor_gradient = np.column_stack([
            np.bincount(items, weights=error * user_factors[users, factor], minlength=item_count)
            for factor in range(rank)
        ]) / item_denominator
        step = learning_rate / (1 + epoch * 0.03)
        user_bias += step * (
            np.bincount(users, weights=error, minlength=user_count) / user_denominator[:, 0]
            - regularization * user_bias
        )
        item_bias += step * (
            np.bincount(items, weights=error, minlength=item_count) / item_denominator[:, 0]
            - regularization * item_bias
        )
        user_factors += step * (user_factor_gradient - regularization * user_factors)
        item_factors += step * (item_factor_gradient - regularization * item_factors)
    return FactorModel(user_bias, item_bias, user_factors, item_factors)


def score_factor_model(data, model):
    scores = (data.global_mean + model.user_bias[:, None] + model.item_bias[None, :]
              + model.user_factors @ model.item_factors.T)
    supported = (data.user_counts[:, None] > 0) & (data.item_counts[None, :] > 0)
    scores = np.where(supported, scores, fallback_matrix(data))
    np.clip(scores, data.rating_min, data.rating_max, out=scores)
    return scores, supported

    users = holdout.user_id.map(data.user_index).to_numpy(dtype=int)
    items = holdout.item_id.map(data.item_index).to_numpy(dtype=int)

    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)

    np.clip(scores, data.rating_min, data.rating_max, out=scores)
    return scores, supported


@dataclass
class FactorModel:
    user_bias: np.ndarray
    item_bias: np.ndarray
    user_factors: np.ndarray
    item_factors: np.ndarray


def fit_factor_model(data, rank=12, regularization=0.05, epochs=40,
                     learning_rate=0.15, seed=42):
    """Regularized, bias-aware factorization fitted on observed train events only."""
    if rank < 1 or epochs < 1 or regularization < 0 or learning_rate <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Invalid factorization hyperparameters")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    user_count, item_count = data.values.shape
    user_factors = rng.normal(0, 0.10, size=(user_count, rank))
    item_factors = rng.normal(0, 0.10, size=(item_count, rank))
    user_bias = np.zeros(user_count)
    item_bias = np.zeros(item_count)
    users, items, ratings = data.event_users, data.event_items, data.event_ratings
    user_denominator = np.maximum(data.user_counts, 1)[:, None]
    item_denominator = np.maximum(data.item_counts, 1)[:, None]
    for epoch in range(epochs):
        estimate = (data.global_mean + user_bias[users] + item_bias[items]
                    + np.sum(user_factors[users] * item_factors[items], axis=1))
        error = ratings - estimate
        user_factor_gradient = np.column_stack([
            np.bincount(users, weights=error * item_factors[items, factor], minlength=user_count)
            for factor in range(rank)
        ]) / user_denominator
        item_factor_gradient = np.column_stack([
            np.bincount(items, weights=error * user_factors[users, factor], minlength=item_count)
            for factor in range(rank)
        ]) / item_denominator
        step = learning_rate / (1 + epoch * 0.03)
        user_bias += step * (
            np.bincount(users, weights=error, minlength=user_count) / user_denominator[:, 0]
            - regularization * user_bias
        )
        item_bias += step * (
            np.bincount(items, weights=error, minlength=item_count) / item_denominator[:, 0]
            - regularization * item_bias
        )
        user_factors += step * (user_factor_gradient - regularization * user_factors)
        item_factors += step * (item_factor_gradient - regularization * item_factors)
    return FactorModel(user_bias, item_bias, user_factors, item_factors)


def score_factor_model(data, model):
    scores = (data.global_mean + model.user_bias[:, None] + model.item_bias[None, :]
              + model.user_factors @ model.item_factors.T)
    supported = (data.user_counts[:, None] > 0) & (data.item_counts[None, :] > 0)
    scores = np.where(supported, scores, fallback_matrix(data))
    np.clip(scores, data.rating_min, data.rating_max, out=scores)
    return scores, supported


def holdout_positions(data, holdout):
    users = holdout.user_id.map(data.user_index).to_numpy(dtype=int)
    items = holdout.item_id.map(data.item_index).to_numpy(dtype=int)
    return users, items


def rating_metrics(data, scores, supported, holdout):
    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)
    truth = holdout.rating.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    predictions = scores[users, items]
    error = predictions - truth
    return {
        "MAE": float(np.mean(np.abs(error))),
        "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(error * error))),
        "prediction_coverage": float(supported[users, items].mean()),
    }


def top_k_items(data, scores, k=10):
    """Rank all catalog items absent from each user's TRAIN history."""
    candidate_scores = scores.copy()
    candidate_scores[data.observed] = -np.inf
    order = np.argsort(-candidate_scores, axis=1, kind="stable")[:, :k]
    return order


def ranking_metrics(data, scores, holdout):
    """Compute both cutoffs from one ranking of unseen training items."""
    cutoffs = (5, 10)
    top_items = top_k_items(data, scores, max(cutoffs))
    relevant = holdout.loc[holdout.rating >= 4, ["user_id", "item_id"]]
    relevance_by_user = {
        data.user_index[int(user_id)]: set(group.item_id.map(data.item_index))
        for user_id, group in relevant.groupby("user_id")
    }
    discounts = 1 / np.log2(np.arange(2, max(cutoffs) + 2))
    per_user = []
    for user_position, user_id in enumerate(data.user_ids):
        positives = relevance_by_user.get(user_position, set())
        if not positives:
            continue
        hits = np.fromiter(
            (item in positives for item in top_items[user_position]),
            dtype=bool, count=max(cutoffs),
        )
        result = {
            "user_id": int(user_id),
            "n_relevant": len(positives),
        }
        for cutoff in cutoffs:
            ideal = discounts[:min(len(positives), cutoff)].sum()
            result[f"Recall@{cutoff}"] = float(hits[:cutoff].sum() / len(positives))
            result[f"NDCG@{cutoff}"] = float(
                (hits[:cutoff] * discounts[:cutoff]).sum() / ideal
            )
        per_user.append(result)
    details = pd.DataFrame(per_user)
    metrics = {key: float(details[key].mean()) for cutoff in cutoffs
               for key in (f"Recall@{cutoff}", f"NDCG@{cutoff}")}
    metrics.update({
        "recommendation_coverage": float(len(np.unique(top_items)) / len(data.item_ids)),
        "ranking_users": len(details),
    })
    return metrics, details


def history_groups(data, scores, holdout, ranking_details):
    """Paired cohorts defined only from train history lengths."""
    boundaries = [-1, 19, 49, 99, np.inf]
    labels = ["1–19", "20–49", "50–99", "100+"]
    user_groups = pd.Series(
        pd.cut(data.user_counts, bins=boundaries, labels=labels),
        index=data.user_ids,
    )
    users, items = holdout_positions(data, holdout)
    prediction_rows = pd.DataFrame({
        "user_id": holdout.user_id.to_numpy(),
        "error": scores[users, items] - holdout.rating.to_numpy(),
    })
    prediction_rows["group"] = prediction_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    ranking_rows = ranking_details.copy()
    ranking_rows["group"] = ranking_rows.user_id.map(user_groups)
    results = []
    for label in labels:
        subset = prediction_rows.loc[prediction_rows.group == label]
        ranked = ranking_rows.loc[ranking_rows.group == label]
        if subset.empty:
            continue
        results.append({
            "train_history": label,
            "users": int((user_groups == label).sum()),
            "test_ratings": len(subset),
            "RMSE": float(np.sqrt(np.mean(subset.error.to_numpy() ** 2))),
            "Recall@5": float(ranked["Recall@5"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
            "NDCG@5": float(ranked["NDCG@5"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
            "Recall@10": float(ranked["Recall@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
            "NDCG@10": float(ranked["NDCG@10"].mean()) if len(ranked) else np.nan,
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(results)


def evaluate_method(data, test, method, neighbor_count=20, common_threshold=50,
                    factor_config=None, return_details=False):
    """Time fitting, prediction and metric computation, excluding data loading."""
    start = perf_counter()
    if method in NEIGHBOR_METHODS:
        similarity = user_similarity(data, method, common_threshold)
        scores, supported = score_neighborhood(data, similarity, neighbor_count)
    elif method == "matrix_factorization":
        model = fit_factor_model(data, **(factor_config or {}))
        scores, supported = score_factor_model(data, model)
    else:
        raise ValueError(method)
    metrics = rating_metrics(data, scores, supported, test)
    rank_metrics, per_user = ranking_metrics(data, scores, test)
    metrics.update(rank_metrics)
    groups = history_groups(data, scores, test, per_user)
    metrics["runtime_seconds"] = perf_counter() - start
    if return_details:
        return metrics, groups, scores, per_user
    return metrics, groups
